title: Clean Action
note: He defines this as work that yields not only wealth but righteousness and fame. Action must be good as well as speech, so this follows the chapter on speech.

couplets.plain: Good allies bring prosperity. Good deeds bring all you want.
couplets.pm: The goodness of your allies gives you wealth alone. The goodness of your actions gives you all you want: righteousness, wealth and pleasure in this life, and the state you desire in the next. So the unseen goodness of action is greater than the visible goodness of allies.

links.quote: Good deeds bring all you want

couplets.plain: Always keep away from work that doesn’t bring good along with fame.
couplets.pm: Ministers must at all times keep clear of work that doesn’t bring their ruler fame in this life and righteousness in the next. He says “always” because good times, bad times and times between all come. “Must” means there is no doing without this.

links.quote: keep away from work that doesn’t bring good along with fame
links.reason: Bars any work that doesn’t bring good along with fame.

couplets.plain: Those who say “We will rise” must stop doing what dims their light.
couplets.pm: Those who mean to rise higher should give up the work that causes their light to fade. Light means being esteemed by everyone in their own time. Anything that dims it isn’t gain.

links.quote: must stop doing what dims their light
links.reason: Anyone wanting to rise must refuse whatever would dim their light.

couplets.plain: Even when they are in trouble, those of unshaken vision won’t do anything shameful.
couplets.pm: Even when trouble comes, those of unshaken clarity won’t escape it by what has shamed those who did it before. They see that you mustn’t take on a disgrace that never passes because of a trouble that soon will, and that even then what is to come will come.

links.reason: Even trouble does not excuse a shameful act.

couplets.plain: Don’t do what will make you cry “What have I done?” If you do, it is good not to do the like again.
couplets.pm: Never do what will later make you grieve, “What have I done?” If in a moment of confusion you do, it is good not to go on grieving afterwards. Everyone will scorn you for it: you know no remedy, you lack firmness, you do useless things, you spread your own shame. He rejects “don’t do the like again” as not fitting the words.
couplets.note: The plain reading takes the second line as “don’t do it again”. He takes it as “don’t go on grieving”, and rejects the other.

links.quote: it is good not to do the like again

couplets.plain: Even if you see the mother who bore you go hungry, don’t do what the worthy condemn.
couplets.pm: Even if poverty brings a man to see the mother who bore him go hungry, he must not do what the wise condemn. The general rule of the law books says that when aged parents, a chaste wife and an infant are starving, you may do many evil things to keep them. That rule doesn’t reach ministers, who follow statecraft, serve rulers and are held in esteem.
couplets.note: The words have no exception. He limits this to ministers, and cites a rule that lets others do evil to feed their dependants.

links.quote: don’t do what the worthy condemn

couplets.plain: Better the deep poverty of the worthy than prosperity gained by wearing disgrace.
couplets.pm: The bitter poverty the worthy endure, refusing disgrace, is higher than the wealth the unworthy win by doing evil and taking disgrace on themselves. To take on lasting disgrace for the sake of passing wealth doesn’t go with worth.

links.quote: the deep poverty of the worthy

couplets.plain: Those who do what is forbidden, not shunning what has been shunned, will find it brings pain even if it succeeds.
couplets.pm: Ministers don’t shun what the learned have forbidden, but do it for wealth. Those deeds aren’t pure, so they won’t succeed. Even if they somehow succeed, they bring only suffering later. To succeed here means to yield the wealth intended.

links.quote: brings pain even if it succeeds

couplets.plain: All that was taken with tears leaves with tears. What is good, even if lost, bears fruit afterwards.
couplets.pm: All the wealth someone takes by evil deeds, making others weep, goes in this life and leaves him weeping. Wealth that came by pure deeds, even if lost at first, comes back later and gives its fruit. “Later” includes the next life.

links.quote: What is good, even if lost, bears fruit afterwards
links.reason: What is good, even when lost for a time, bears fruit afterwards.

couplets.plain: Trying to stay safe on wealth made by deceit is like pouring water into a pot of raw clay and keeping it there.
couplets.pm: A minister who makes wealth by evil deeds to keep his ruler safe is like one who pours water into a pot of raw clay to keep it safe. Such deeds are deceit because they seem to bring gain and then bring ruin. Ruler and wealth perish together. He rejects the text ஏமாத்தல், “rejoicing”, because it breaks the comparison.

links.quote: pouring water into a pot of raw clay
